video.title: You Can Feel This - Here's How

classification.reason: The coach provides actionable mental cues and kinesthetic checks to drive shoulders forward and pull the hip backward to load core tension.

problem.title_as_question: How should the hips and pelvis work during the forehand, and what should you actually feel?
problem.definition: Explaining the apparent paradox where the pelvis physically accelerates forward yet the player must feel or intend to pull the hip backward to stretch the core fascia and transfer energy.
prerequisites: Coiling the upper body against the lower body on the forehand
problem.target_player: Players who attempt to drive their hitting hip forward through the shot and end up rotating their upper and lower body together as a block.

symptoms.description: The shoulders and hips rotate together as a block rather than rotating opposite each other under tension.
Lack of stretch tension felt across the diagonal core and fascial chain between the hip and opposite shoulder.
The pelvis continues rotating forward through the shot without stopping to let the shoulders overtake it.

causes.statement: The external oblique and fascial chain connecting the hip and shoulder creates an equal and opposite tension that flings the shoulder forward while pulling the hip backward.
The pelvis accelerates forward initially solely to pre-stretch and maximize tension across this connecting fascial line before releasing the shoulders.
Consciously trying to push the hitting hip forward through the shot causes the player to avoid stretching the core fascia, resulting in hips and shoulders rotating together.
The backward force from the unwinding fascia causes backward acceleration that decelerates and stops the forward-moving pelvis rather than visibly reversing its direction.

angles.summary: The external oblique and connected fascial chain stretch and unstretch to transfer energy between the pelvis and shoulders.
A corkscrew tool with hip and shoulder anchors illustrates how twisting forces on one anchor create opposite tension on the other.
Demonstrating how trying to push the hip far forward is only possible when upper body resistance is removed, proving it kills fascial tension.
Explaining that the cue to drive the right hip through the shot misleads players because human brains perceive acceleration and tension rather than absolute position.

solutions.summary: Intend to take the hitting side hip and fire or pull it backwards as you begin the forward swing.
Use the combined cue to 'drive shoulders forward, hips back' when coiled and about to swing to maximize diagonal tension.
Check for the exact transition moment where the pelvis feels yanked backwards while the shoulders are yanked forward.
Check that the pelvis feels under tension getting pulled backwards and slowing down rather than rotating freely through the shot.
